cues.en: One thing that I really like about the causal approach is that it allows us to ask questions about counterfactuals.
cues.zh: 我很喜歡因果方法的一點，是它讓我們能提出反事實問題。

cues.en: A counterfactual is asking the question what would happen if something had been different?
cues.zh: 反事實就是問：如果某件事不同，會發生什麼？

cues.en: You can ask these kinds of questions about your life and decisions you've made.
cues.zh: 可以對自己的人生，以及做過的決定，提出這類問題。

cues.en: For example, what would your life be like now if you hadn't enrolled in this course?
cues.zh: 例如，如果沒有報名這門課，你現在的人生會是什麼樣子？

cues.en: Well, in real life we cannot run experiments like that.
cues.zh: 現實生活中，我們無法做那種實驗。

cues.en: But with language models, we actually can.
cues.zh: 但語言模型就真的可以。

cues.en: We can ask what token the model would predict if we had manipulated the context in different ways.
cues.zh: 我們可以問，如果以不同方式操作上下文，模型會預測哪個 token？

cues.en: There are three sources of difficulties in causal interpretability research.
cues.zh: 因果可解釋性研究的困難，有三個來源。

cues.en: The first is that there are just so many moving parts inside a model, so many neurons and dimensions
cues.zh: 第一，模型內部有太多互相作用的部分，太多神經元、維度、

cues.en: and attention heads and transformer blocks and so on, that there's just limitless possibilities for parts of the model to manipulate.
cues.zh: 注意力頭與 Transformer 區塊等等，所以，可以操作的模型部分幾乎無窮無盡。

cues.en: And then you need to decide whether to zero out the activations, replace them with some other value like the average or the median.
cues.zh: 接著，還得決定要把活化歸零，或換成平均數、中位數等其他值。

cues.en: Add noise or replace entirely with noise.
cues.zh: 加入雜訊，或者完全替換成雜訊。

cues.en: You can also take the activations or the embeddings vectors from one model and insert them into another model.
cues.zh: 也可以把一個模型的活化或嵌入向量，放進另一個模型。

cues.en: There's just so many possibilities that it can be challenging to focus the analyses onto a very small number of key experiments to run.
cues.zh: 可能性實在太多，因此，要把分析集中於少數關鍵實驗，可能很困難。

cues.en: A second challenge is just a difficulty that is present in all complex systems.
cues.zh: 第二個挑戰，是所有複雜系統都存在的困難。

cues.en: The representations and computations that take place inside a language model are distributed.
cues.zh: 語言模型內部的表徵與計算，是分散的。

cues.en: They are multidimensional, possibly spanning multiple spatial scales, multiple different layers of the model.
cues.zh: 它們是多維的，可能跨越多個空間尺度、模型的多個不同層。

cues.en: And there are also mechanisms that are specifically built into the model to compensate for disruptions.
cues.zh: 而且，模型中還特別建立了補償干擾的機制。

cues.en: And part of that is the various layer normalizations, which can compensate for changes in activation magnitudes or distributional shifts.
cues.zh: 其中一部分，是各種層正規化，能補償活化量值的改變或分布偏移。

cues.en: And also part of that is that the models have specifically been trained to be robust to aberrant patterns being injected into the neurons.
cues.zh: 另一部分，是模型已經特別訓練過，要能穩健應對注入神經元的異常模式。

cues.en: Here I'm referring in particular to dropout regularization.
cues.zh: 這裡特別指的是 dropout 正規化。

cues.en: So when you do dropout during training, you are literally just zeroing out certain parts of the model.
cues.zh: 訓練時做 dropout，真的就是把模型某些部分歸零。

cues.en: And the model has to learn to deal with that and be robust to those manipulations.
cues.zh: 模型必須學會處理這種情況，並對那些操作保持穩健。

cues.en: So then you do causal manipulations where you zero out some activation patterns, and the model has literally learned to deal with patterns like that during training.
cues.zh: 因此，當你做因果操作，把某些活化模式歸零時，模型其實早在訓練期間，就已經學過如何應對這類模式。

cues.en: A third source of difficulty is the lack of ground truth to verify the results that you get.
cues.zh: 第三個困難來源，是缺乏能驗證結果的真值。

cues.en: This is actually a bit better than the lack of ground truth with the observational methods, because
cues.zh: 這其實比觀察式方法缺乏真值的情況好一點，因為

cues.en: at least with intervention experiments you can do like parametric manipulations, for example, manipulating
cues.zh: 至少在干預實驗中，可以做參數化操作，例如輪流操作

cues.en: the different heads in turn, or scaling activation patterns by different amounts.
cues.zh: 不同注意力頭，或用不同幅度縮放活化模式。

cues.en: And of course, you can see how the causal manipulations impact the model predictions and the text that it generates.
cues.zh: 當然，也能觀察因果操作如何影響模型預測與產生的文字。

cues.en: All that said, I don't mean to suggest that this kind of research is impossible or that progress cannot be made.

cues.en: The field is new and developing quickly.
cues.zh: 這個領域很新，而且快速發展。

cues.en: Experiments and theories, ideas, interpretations are all getting better, more precise and more sophisticated.
cues.zh: 實驗、理論、想法與解讀，都在變得更好、更精確、更成熟。

cues.en: But the good thing for you is that the foundational techniques are the same, and probably will be for a long time.
cues.zh: 對你來說，好消息是，基礎技術相同，而且很可能會維持很長一段時間。

cues.en: The electrical grid in Amsterdam is specifically engineered so that when there is a disruption in the flow of electricity somewhere.

cues.zh: 最終結果完全相同。

cues.en: In other words, the local disruptions are completely compensated for by this network architecture.
cues.zh: 換句話說，這個網路架構完全補償了局部干擾。

cues.en: And this is something to think about with complex systems.
cues.zh: 思考複雜系統時，可以記住這點。

cues.en: Causal manipulations are important in science, but they can be tricky to interpret for multiple reasons.
cues.zh: 因果操作在科學上很重要，但有很多原因，會讓它們難以解讀。

cues.en: And so they should be seen as complementary methods along with the non-causal approaches that you are
